walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium to find normal reaction $R$:
$$R + X\sin\alpha - mg = 0$$
$$R + 0.28X - 300(10) = 0 \implies R = 3000 - 0.28X$$

Resolve forces horizontally for limiting equilibrium ($F = X\cos\alpha$):
$$F = 0.96X$$

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Resolves vertically to get $R = 3000 - 0.28X$, horizontally to get $F = 0.96X$, uses $F = 0.5R$, and solves to find $X = 1360\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the trigonometric components of the applied force $X$:
Given $\sin\alpha = 0.28$:
$$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2\alpha} = \sqrt{1 - (0.28)^2} = \sqrt{1 - 0.0784} = \sqrt{0.9216} = 0.96$$

Identify all forces acting on the crate:
- Downward gravitational weight: $W = mg = (300)(10) = 3000\text{ N}$
- Upward normal reaction from the ground: $R$
- Applied force $X$ at angle $lpha$ above the horizontal: horizontal component $+X\cos\alpha$, vertical component $+X\sin\alpha$
- Opposing horizontal friction force: $F$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium (since there is no vertical motion):
$$\sum F_{\text{vertical}} = 0$$
$$R + X\sin\alpha - W = 0$$
$$R + 0.28X - 3000 = 0$$
Rearrange to express $R$ in terms of $X$:
$$R = 3000 - 0.28X$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$\sum F_{\text{horizontal}} = 0$$
$$X\cos\alpha - F = 0$$
$$F = 0.96X$$

At the point of slipping, the crate is in limiting equilibrium, so friction reaches its maximum value:
$$F = \mu R$$
Substitute $\mu = 0.5$, $F = 0.96X$, and $R = 3000 - 0.28X$:
$$0.96X = 0.5(3000 - 0.28X)$$
Expand the right-hand side:
$$0.96X = 1500 - 0.14X$$
Add $0.14X$ to both sides:
$$0.96X + 0.14X = 1500$$
$$1.10X = 1500$$
Divide both sides by $1.10$:
$$X = \frac{1500}{1.10} = \frac{15\,000}{11} \approx 1363.64\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $X = 1360\text{ N}$.
